mainTopic: תפילין: the ברכות, the order of putting on and taking off, and the times for wearing them
overview: רב חסדא rules that if someone talks between putting on the arm תפילין and the head תפילין, he must say a ברכה again. The גמרא asks how this fits with רבי יוחנן, who gives a separate ברכה for each one. אביי and רבא answer that without talking you say one ברכה, and after talking you say two. A ברייתא adds that talking in between is a sin, serious enough to send a man home from the army. Another ברייתא teaches the order: put on the arm תפילין first and take off the head תפילין first. The arm-first rule comes from the order of the פסוק, and רבה learns from 'והיו' that while the head תפילין is on, both must be on. A further ברייתא teaches that the ברכה is said when the time for the מצוה arrives, and then gives three opinions on how late תפילין may be worn. רב נחמן's ruling on רבי יעקב's view is reported in two opposite versions.

steps.title: Talking between the two תפילין requires a new blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that someone who talked between the arm and head תפילין must say a ברכה again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: If someone talked between putting on one תפילין and the other, he goes back and says a blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling from רב חסדא. Talking in the middle of putting on תפילין means you must say a ברכה again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The arm תפילין and head תפילין are normally treated as one connected act under one ברכה. Talking breaks that connection, so the head תפילין needs its own ברכה. This step only sets the rule. The next step will question what it implies.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the תפילין (singular): the arm one or the head one
Goes back and says the blessing again

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
If one spoke between one tefillah and the other tefillah,
phrases.notes: He means between putting on the arm תפילין and putting on the head תפילין.

phrases.english: he goes back and recites a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about interrupting while putting on תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Talking between the arm and head תפילין requires saying a ברכה again.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the head תפילין always gets its own blessing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads רב חסדא as saying that without talking there is no ברכה on the head תפילין. It then challenges this from רבי יוחנן, who gives a separate ברכה for each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he talked, yes, he says a blessing. If he did not talk, no blessing? But רב חייא son of רב הונא sent a ruling in the name of רבי יוחנן: on the arm תפילין one says 'Blessed... Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to put on תפילין.' On the head תפילין one says 'Blessed... Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us about the commandment of תפילין.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from רב חסדא's words. It then attacks that inference with a ruling of רבי יוחנן that seems to require a ברכה on the head תפילין every time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's wording suggests that only after talking does the head תפילין get a ברכה. But רבי יוחנן lists two different ברכות, one for each תפילין, with no condition about talking. So it looks like the head תפילין always gets its own ברכה, which clashes with the inference from רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)
To put on תפילין: the ברכה on the arm תפילין
About the commandment of תפילין: the ברכה on the head תפילין

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not against רב חסדא's actual ruling about talking. It is against what his words imply: that without talking there is no ברכה on the head תפילין.

phrases.english: If he spoke, yes; if he did not speak, no?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is reading between the lines of רב חסדא: does this mean that without talking, there is no ברכה on the head תפילין?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא שְׁלַח רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: But Rav Chiyya, son of Rav Huna, sent
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
On the tefillah of the arm one says:
"Blessed... Who has sanctified us with His commandments
and commanded us to put on tefillin."
On the tefillin of the head one says:
"Blessed... Who has sanctified us with His commandments
and commanded us concerning the commandment of tefillin."

steps.triggerLanguage: סָח – אִין, לֹא סָח – לָא? וְהָא שְׁלַח רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what רב חסדא's ruling implies.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from רב חסדא that without talking, the head תפילין gets no ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן gives a separate ברכה for the head תפילין with no mention of talking, so it seems the head always gets its own ברכה.

steps.title: One blessing without talking, two blessings after talking
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא explain that רבי יוחנן's second ברכה is only said when the person talked. Without talking, one ברכה covers both.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both say: if he did not talk, he says one blessing. If he talked, he says two blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי and רבא answer the question. They read רבי יוחנן as describing the case where the person talked in between.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without talking, the single ברכה 'להניח תפילין' covers both תפילין. After talking, the connection is broken, so he also says 'על מצות תפילין' on the head. This makes רבי יוחנן agree with רב חסדא.
steps.whatToRemember: Without talking: one ברכה (להניח) covers both תפילין. With talking in between: two ברכות, one on each.

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava both say:
If he did not speak, he recites one blessing;
if he spoke, he recites two blessings.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: רבי יוחנן's two ברכות apply only when the person talked.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן means the head תפילין always gets its own ברכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two ברכות only after talking. Otherwise one ברכה covers both, just as רב חסדא implied.

steps.title: Talking in between is a sin
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that talking between the two תפילין is a sin. Because of it, a man is sent back from the army.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if someone talked between one תפילין and the other, he has a sin in his hand, and because of it he returns home from the ranks of war.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing how serious it is to talk between the two תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Talking in between does more than force an extra ברכה. It counts as an עבירה. This sin is serious enough to make him one of the men sent back from battle.

keyTerms.meaning: He has a sin in his hand: he is guilty of a sin
The lines or ranks of battle

steps.whyThisMatters: Even though the extra ברכה 'fixes' the interruption, one should not talk between putting on the arm and head תפילין in the first place.

phrases.english: It was taught: If one spoke between one tefillah and the other tefillah,
it is a sin in his hand,
and because of it he returns from the ranks of war.
phrases.notes: This points to דברים 20:8, where the man who is afraid is sent home before battle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא about how serious it is to talk in the case רב חסדא discussed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Talking between the arm and head תפילין is a sin, serious enough to send a man home from war.

steps.title: Arm first when putting on, head first when taking off
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the order: put on the של יד and then the של ראש. Take off the של ראש and then the של יד.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: when a person puts on תפילין, he puts on the arm one and then the head one. When he takes them off, he takes off the head one and then the arm one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the order of putting on and taking off the two תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order flips. Putting on goes arm, then head. Taking off goes head, then arm. This sets up the גמרא's next question: where does each half of this rule come from?

keyTerms.meaning: The arm תפילין / the head תפילין

phrases.english: It was taught: when he puts on (תפילין),
he puts on the arm one,
and afterward he puts on the head one;
and when he takes them off, he takes off the head one,
and afterward he takes off the arm one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ברייתא about the two תפילין, this time about their order
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Put on arm then head; take off head then arm.

steps.title: The order for putting on is clear, but where does the order for taking off come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the putting-on order comes straight from the פסוק, which mentions the arm before the head. It then asks for a source for the taking-off order.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the arm one goes on first, because the פסוק first says 'bind them as a sign on your arm' and then says 'they shall be frontlets between your eyes.' But taking off the head one first and then the arm one: where do we learn that from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the first half of the ברייתא because the פסוק supports it. Then it asks for a source for the second half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק's order (arm, then head) explains the putting-on order. That same order would seem to say nothing about taking off, and if anything you might expect to take them off in the same order. So the reversed order for taking off needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (one part is understood, another part is not)
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: It makes sense that when he puts on,

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּיחַ שֶׁל יָד וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַנִּיחַ שֶׁל רֹאשׁ,
phrases.english: he puts on the arm one and afterward the head one,
since it is written: "And you shall bind them as a sign on your arm,"
and afterward: "and they shall be frontlets between your eyes."
But when he takes them off,

phrases.aramaic: חוֹלֵץ שֶׁל רֹאשׁ וְאַחַר כָּךְ חוֹלֵץ שֶׁל יָד,
phrases.english: that he takes off the head one and afterward the arm one,
from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source of each half of the ברייתא in step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for removing the head תפילין before the arm תפילין

steps.title: While the head תפילין is on, both must be on
steps.stepSummary: רבה, quoting רב הונא, reads the פסוק to mean that as long as the head תפילין is between your eyes, there must be two. So the head one has to come off first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: רב הונא explained it to me. The פסוק says 'and they shall be frontlets between your eyes.' This teaches that the whole time they are between your eyes, there should be two.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question with a reading of the פסוק that he learned from רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'they' (והיו) is plural. So while the head תפילין is on, both תפילין should be on. If you took off the arm one first, the head one would be left alone. That is why the head one comes off first.
steps.whatToRemember: Arm on first, because the פסוק lists it first. Head off first, so that the head תפילין is never on without the arm one.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה: רַב הוּנָא אַסְבְּרַאּ לִי,
phrases.english: רבה said: רב הונא explained it to me:
The פסוק says: "And they shall be frontlets between your eyes,"
the whole time that it is between your eyes,
there should be two.
phrases.notes: So you take off the head one first. That way the head one is never on by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: רַב הוּנָא אַסְבְּרַאּ לִי
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'והיו' (plural) teaches that while the head תפילין is on, both must be on, so the head one comes off first.

steps.title: The ברכה is said when the time for תפילין arrives
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches when to say the ברכה on תפילין. Someone who put them on early, before the proper time, touches them and says the ברכה when the time arrives.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: from when does one say a ברכה on תפילין? From the time of putting them on. How does this work? If someone got up early to travel and was afraid his תפילין would get lost, he puts them on. When their time comes, he touches them and says the ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא asks at what point the ברכה on תפילין is said, and gives a case to explain the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case shows that 'the time of putting them on' means the time for the מצוה, not just whenever they happen to go on your body. The traveler wore them before their time only to keep them safe. So he holds off the ברכה until the proper time arrives, and then he touches them and says it.

keyTerms.meaning: From the time of putting them on

steps.confusionAlert: Here, 'from the time of putting them on' does not mean the ברכה is said whenever they go on. The case shows it is said when the time for the מצוה arrives.

phrases.english: The רבנן taught: תפילין,
from when does one say a ברכה on them?
From the time of putting them on.
phrases.notes: The case right after this shows it means the proper time for the מצוה.

phrases.english: How so?
If he was getting up early to set out on the road
and is afraid they might get lost, he puts them on;
and when their time arrives,
he touches them and says a ברכה on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: תְּפִילִּין מֵאֵימָתַי מְבָרֵךְ עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא, now about the timing of the ברכה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה on תפילין is said when the time for the מצוה arrives. If they were put on early, one touches them and says the ברכה then.

steps.title: Until when are תפילין worn? Three opinions
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. The first opinion says תפילין are worn until sunset. רבי יעקב says until people stop walking in the marketplace. חכמים say until bedtime.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until when does one wear them? Until the sun sets. רבי יעקב says: until people stop walking in the marketplace. חכמים say: until the time of sleep.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא now moves from the start of the day to the end. It asks how late one may wear תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three opinions, from earliest to latest. The first is sunset. Next is רבי יעקב, when the marketplace empties out. The latest is חכמים, bedtime.

keyTerms.meaning: When people stop walking in the marketplace

phrases.english: And until when does he wear them?
Until the sun sets.
רבי יעקב says:
Until people stop walking in the marketplace;
and חכמים say: until the time of sleep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא moves from the start time to the end time
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three opinions on the end time: sunset, the emptying of the marketplace (רבי יעקב), and bedtime (חכמים).

steps.title: חכמים agree: once they are off and the sun sets, don't put them back on
steps.stepSummary: חכמים agree with רבי יעקב about one case. If someone took off his תפילין to use the bathroom or go into the bathhouse, and the sun set meanwhile, he does not put them back on.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים agree with רבי יעקב that if he took them off to go to the bathroom or to enter the bathhouse, and the sun set, he does not go back and put them on again.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a point of agreement. Even חכמים, who allow wearing תפילין until bedtime, agree about this one case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים allow you to keep wearing תפילין that are already on after sunset. But if they came off and the sun set in the meantime, everyone agrees you do not put them back on.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not go back again

steps.whatToRemember: Bless when the time for the מצוה arrives. The end time is a מחלוקת, but once תפילין are off and the sun has set, they are not put back on.

phrases.english: And חכמים agree with רבי יעקב
that if he took them off to go out to the bathroom
or to enter the bathhouse,
and the sun set,
he does not go back and put them on again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the מחלוקת of step 9 with a case everyone agrees on
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If תפילין were removed and the sun set in the meantime, they are not put back on, even according to חכמים.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules like רבי יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the הלכה follows רבי יעקב: תפילין may be worn until people stop walking in the marketplace.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The הלכה is like רבי יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: After the ברייתא's three opinions, an אמורא steps in to tell us which one we follow in practice. רב נחמן says we follow רבי יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא left an open argument about how late תפילין may be worn. רב נחמן picks the middle view: later than sunset, but not as late as bedtime. This is the first version of his ruling. A different version comes in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows this opinion

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
The halakha is like Rabbi Yaakov.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument presented in the ברייתא (steps 9–10).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יעקב: תפילין are worn until people stop walking in the marketplace.

steps.title: Two sages prayed the evening prayer wearing תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא used to pray in the evening while wearing תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא would pray with them, with the תפילין, in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how two אמוראים actually behaved. They wore תפילין while praying the evening prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This report shows that wearing תפילין after sunset was done in practice. That fits the first version of רב נחמן's ruling, that we may follow רבי יעקב and wear them past sunset. It is a real-life example rather than a formal proof.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna
would pray with them in the evening.
phrases.notes: "With them" means while wearing the תפילין.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא מְצַלּוּ בְּהוּ בְּאוּרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical example that matches רב נחמן's ruling in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, these sages wore תפילין past sunset, during the evening prayer.

steps.title: A second version: the הלכה is not like רבי יעקב
steps.stepSummary: Some report רב נחמן's ruling the opposite way: the הלכה is NOT like רבי יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רב נחמן said: The הלכה is not like רבי יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of what רב נחמן said. In this version, he rules against רבי יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are now two versions of רב נחמן's ruling, and they say opposite things. In the second version we do not extend the time for תפילין to when people leave the marketplace. That leaves the earlier view that the time ends at sunset.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law does not follow this opinion

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new sage arguing with רב נחמן. It is a different report of what רב נחמן himself said.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רב נחמן's ruling. One says the הלכה is like רבי יעקב (until the marketplace empties), and one says it is not.

phrases.english: Some say:
The halakha is not like Rabbi Yaakov.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, opposite version of רב נחמן's ruling in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, the הלכה does not follow רבי יעקב.
